info.title: AbyssHub API
info.summary: Run any AbyssHub Widget from your code or your agent.
info.description:
Run an AbyssHub Widget from code: press it with an input and get back the ended run, in one call.

## The key

Send an API Key on every request as `Authorization: Bearer abyss_sk_…`. Create one in your Cave. A key acts as you: its runs are paid from your wallet and are private to you. Read it from an environment variable such as `ABYSS_API_KEY`; never write it into code. A key is a server-side secret, so `/v1` sends no CORS headers and no browser can call it.

## One call

Every Widget, every run length, the same code:

1. `GET /v1/widgets/{id}` tells you the `price` you pay and the `input_schema` your input must match.
2. Press: `POST /v1/widgets/{id}/runs` with `{"input": {…}}`. The press holds until the run ends: `200` and its headers, `Location` among them, come at once, then a space every 2 seconds while the run goes on, then the run once `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`. JSON allows the leading spaces, so any JSON parser reads the answer. The code goes out before the ending is known: read `status`, never the HTTP status, to learn how the run ended.

The same call serves a 3-second run and a 30-minute run.

## Long runs

A hold can end early with the run as it is, still `queued` or `running`: after an hour, or when the API is busy, when the press answers `202` at once. A deploy can cut a hold too. Then read the run at its `Location` with `GET /v1/runs/{id}?wait=true`, which holds the same way. If you got no headers at all, press again with the same `Idempotency-Key`: the repeat holds too.

To start a run without waiting, send `"wait": false` with the press. It answers `202` at once with the run `queued`; read it with `?wait=true` when you want its ending.

## Files

A file Field takes an `https` URL on a public address, which the API fetches at the press, or the `id` of an upload from `POST /v1/widgets/{id}/uploads`. Or send the file itself in the press, as a form: `curl -F report=@report.pdf -F note=hello`. A finished run lists what it wrote in `output_files`. Each `url` there is signed fresh on every read and expires: re-read the run, never store a URL.

## Errors

A failure is `{"error": {"code", "message", "param"?, "doc_url", …}, "request_id"}`. Branch on `error.code`, never on the status or the `message`: the message is written for a person and may change, the code never does. Every code, its status and what to do about it is listed in `components.schemas.ErrorCode`. Every response carries a `Request-Id` header; quote it to support.

## Retrying safely

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header with a press and you may retry it after a timeout or a dropped connection: a retry with the same key and the same body answers like the first press, with that press's run and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`: it holds, or answers `202` at once with `"wait": false`. It never runs or charges twice. Reading a run is always safe to retry. On `429 rate_limited` and `409 idempotency_key_in_use`, wait the `Retry-After` seconds; no other failure sends it.

## Versioning

The version is the `/v1` path; there is no version header. Within `/v1` fields, codes and optional parameters are only ever added. Nothing is renamed, removed or given a new meaning. Ignore the fields and codes you don't know. A breaking change would be `/v2`, beside `/v1`.

get.summary: The API Key you are sending
get.description: What the key on this request is, whose it is, and what it has spent this calendar month (UTC) against its Spend Cap. Use it to check a key before you press anything.

get.summary: A Widget, before you press it
get.description: What the Widget does, the one price you pay for a run, your Free Runs on it, and the exact input it takes as JSON Schema. Read it once before your first press, and again if a press answers `invalid_input` or `price_above_max`.

example.name: Chart Maker
example.description: Turns a CSV into a bar chart.

data.description:
CSV file

An https URL or an upload id.

post.summary: Upload a local file for a file Field
post.description: For a file that is not at a public `https` URL. Name the file Field and the file; the answer is an `id` and an S3 upload form. Send the form as `multipart/form-data` to `upload.url`: every entry of `upload.fields` first, then the file itself as `file`. Then press with the `id` as that Field's value. The id is yours alone, for this Widget, and the upload goes straight to storage, never through this API.

200.description: The upload's id and the form to send the file with.

post.summary: Press: run a Widget and wait for its ending
post.description:
Starts one run and holds until it ends: `200`, `Location` and the other headers at once, then a space every 2 seconds, then the run once `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`. Read `status` to learn how it ended. After an hour the hold answers the run as it is, `running`; read it again at its `Location` with `?wait=true`.

The body is JSON, or a form (`multipart/form-data`) with one part per Field, so a local file goes in the same call. A form always holds.

With `"wait": false` in a JSON body, or when the API's holds are all taken, the press answers `202` at once with the run `queued`.

The checks run in this order, and every refusal comes before the charge, so a refused press costs nothing: the key, the Widget, the `Idempotency-Key`, the body and the input, a form's files and the URLs your file Fields name, `max_price`, the key's Spend Cap, then your wallet.

The run costs the Widget's `price` from `GET /v1/widgets/{id}`. A failed run is refunded.

200.description: The run once it has ended, `succeeded` or `failed`, or as it is after an hour's hold, `running`. The status and the headers come at once and the body after the hold, preceded by a space every 2 seconds. A replay of an earlier press holds the same way, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

202.description: The run, as the press accepted it: always `queued`. Sent when the body has `"wait": false`, or at once when the API's holds are all taken. A replay of an earlier press (same `Idempotency-Key`, same body) answers that press's run as it is now, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.description: The runs made through `/v1` by any of your keys, newest first, a page at a time, so you can find a run whose id you lost. Runs from the website are not listed. There are no filters and no totals: while `has_more` is true, ask for the next page with `starting_after` set to the last run's `id`.

200.description: A page of runs, each as it is now.

get.summary: Read a run, or wait for its ending
get.description:
The run as it is now, at once. With `?wait=true` the read holds as the press does: `200` at once, then a space every 2 seconds, then the run once `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`, or as it is after an hour's hold. When the API's holds are all taken it answers at once.

Re-read the run whenever you need its files: each `output_files[].url` is signed fresh on every read and expires, so never store one.

200.description: The run, as it is now or, with `?wait=true`, once it has ended.

get.description: The `/v1` contract as OpenAPI 3.1. It needs no key.

ApiKey.description: An API Key, as `Authorization: Bearer abyss_sk_…`. Create one in your Cave; it is shown once. A missing, unknown or revoked key, or a website sign-in token, is `401 invalid_api_key`.

WidgetId.name: id
WidgetId.description: The Widget's id, `widget_` and its number (as in `widget_1660`), or the private token of an unlisted Widget you were given the private link to. Nothing else names a Widget.

RunId.name: id
RunId.description: The run's `id`, `run_` and 24 characters, as the press answered it.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes the press safe to retry. Any 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters; a UUID is a good choice, new for each new press. The key is kept for 24 hours and is yours alone. A retry with the same key and the same body answers like the first press, with its run and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`: it holds, or answers `202` at once with `"wait": false`. It never runs or charges twice. The same key with a different body is `422 idempotency_key_reused`; the same key while the first press is still being handled is `409 idempotency_key_in_use`. A refused press is not kept, so fix the request and send it again with the same key.

Wait.name: wait
Wait.description: `true` holds the read until the run ends, as the press holds: `200` at once, a space every 2 seconds, then the run. After an hour, or when the API's holds are all taken, it answers the run as it is, so read again while `status` is `queued` or `running`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many runs to answer, 1 to 100.

StartingAfter.name: starting_after
StartingAfter.description: The `id` of the last run on the page you have: the page answered starts after it.

RequestId.description: This request's id, on every response. Quote it to support; it is also the `request_id` in an error.

RetryAfter.description: How many seconds to wait before sending the request again.

Location.description: Where the run is read: `GET /v1/runs/{id}`. After a cut hold, read it there with `?wait=true`.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when this answer replays an earlier press with the same `Idempotency-Key`; absent otherwise.

BadRequest.description: The press was refused by a limit you set, and nothing was charged: `spend_cap_reached` or `price_above_max`. Retrying the same request will not help.

error.message: This run costs 3.1 Ƀ, more than the max_price you sent. Nothing was charged. Check the price (GET /v1/widgets/{id}), then press again with a higher max_price or none.

Unauthorized.description: `invalid_api_key`: the key is missing, unknown or revoked, or a website sign-in token was sent instead.

error.message: Send a live API Key as "Authorization: Bearer abyss_sk_…". Create one in your Cave; a revoked key, or a website sign-in, is not accepted here.

PaymentRequired.description: `insufficient_funds`: your wallet can't cover the price; `shortfall` says by how much. Nothing was charged.

error.message: Your Available Byssium is 0.3 Ƀ short of this run's price. Top up your wallet, then press again.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: this key can't see the Widget or run, or nothing is at this path. A run is readable only when it was made through `/v1` by one of your keys.

error.message: There is nothing at this address that this API Key can see.

Conflict.description: `idempotency_key_in_use`: the first press with this `Idempotency-Key` is still being handled. Wait the `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request again to get its run.

UnprocessableContent.description: The request can't be taken as sent, and nothing was charged: `invalid_request`, `invalid_input`, `input_unreachable`, `idempotency_key_reused` or a `held_input_*` code. `param` names the part at fault.

error.message: The input does not match this Widget's input_schema (GET /v1/widgets/{id}): The title field is required.

TooManyRequests.description: `rate_limited`: this key sent too many requests this minute, across all of `/v1`. Wait the `Retry-After` seconds.

ServerError.description: `server_error`: the platform's fault. Try again; quote the `request_id` if it keeps happening.

Byssium.description: An amount of Byssium (Ƀ), the platform's currency, to the hundredth.

Timestamp.description: A moment in UTC, ISO 8601 with a `Z`.

Key.description: An API Key, as the caller holding it sees it. Never its secret.

name.description: The name you gave the key.

key.description: The key's display form: its prefix and last four characters.

user.description: The person the key acts as. Its runs are theirs.

spend_cap.description: The most this key may spend in a calendar month (UTC), or null when it has no cap. A press that would pass it is `400 spend_cap_reached`.

spent_this_month.description: The `price` of this key's runs this calendar month (UTC): what its Spend Cap is held to.

Widget.description: A Widget, as the caller about to press it sees it.

id.description: The Widget's id, for the paths.

description.description: What the Widget does, as plain text: no markup, a newline between paragraphs. Null when the Widget has none.

url.description: The Widget's page on the website.

price.description: The one price you pay for a run: the Widget's price for you plus the Call Price. A Free Run costs only the Call Price. It is what `max_price` is checked against.

free_runs.description: Your Free Runs on this Widget, never folded into `price`; null for your own Widget and for a free one.

InputSchema.description: The input this Widget takes, as a JSON Schema 2020-12 object: one property per Field, keyed by the Field's name. Validate your `input` against it before you press. A file Field is a string, an `https` URL or an upload `id`, or a list of them for a multi-file Field. A date Field is `YYYY-MM-DD`. A key that is not a Field is refused.

UploadRequest.description: Which file Field the file is for, and its name. Nothing else is taken.

field.description: The file Field's name, as in `input_schema`.

filename.description: The file's name; its extension must be one the Field takes.

size.description: The file's size in bytes. Given, a file over the Field's limit is refused now rather than at the upload.

Upload.description: An upload: the id to put in `input`, and the form that sends the file.

id.description: The upload's id: the value of its file Field at the press.

upload.description: An S3 POST form. Send `multipart/form-data` to `url` with every entry of `fields`, then the file as `file`. It expires within the hour.

PressRequest.description: A press. An empty body is an empty input. Any other key is refused with `invalid_request`.

input.description: The Widget's Fields by name, matching its `input_schema`. A key that is not a Field is `invalid_input`.

max_price.description: The most you will pay for this run. If the Widget's `price` has risen above it, the press is `400 price_above_max` and nothing is charged.

wait.description: `false` answers `202` at once with the run `queued`, without waiting for its ending. Left out, the press holds until the run ends.

PressForm.description:
A press as a form, so cURL, or a language with no library, sends a local file in one call: `curl -F report=@report.pdf -F note=hello`. Each part is one Field, named by the Field's name.

A file part is held for the run under your own uploads, to the Field's `maxFileSizeMB`, else 512 MB; a file the Field refuses is `held_input_*`, with `param` naming the Field. A text part is the Field's value as text: a number Field takes `250000`, a date `2026-10-05`, a choice its option, and a file Field an `https` URL or an upload id. A list repeats the name with `[]`: `-F "tags[]=a" -F "tags[]=b"`, or `-F "photos[]=@a.png" -F "photos[]=@b.png"`.

A form carries input only. A part that names no Field is `invalid_input`, with `param` naming it; `max_price` goes in a JSON body. An `Idempotency-Key` works with a form as with JSON: the same parts, with the same files, replay.

anyOf.description: A text part: the Field's value as text.
A file part, for a file Field.
A list: the part's name repeated with `[]`.

Run.description: A run. Read it again to see it move: fields are only ever added to it.

widget.description: The id of the Widget it ran.

status.description: Where the run is. Read again while it is `queued` or `running`; `succeeded` and `failed` are final. A status never moves backwards: once a run reads `running`, it never reads `queued` again.

oneOf.description: Waiting to start, in line behind your other runs included.
Building, starting or running.
Ended well: read `result` and `output_files`.
Ended badly and refunded: read `error`.

price.description: What this run cost you, and `0` once it failed, because a failed run is refunded. The sum over your runs is exactly what you spent.

result.description: Once the run succeeded, the JSON the Widget wrote to `output/output.json`, if it wrote one; null otherwise. Any JSON value.

output_files.description: The files the run wrote, empty until it ends.

error.description: Why the run failed, once it has; null otherwise.

started_at.description: When it first left `queued`; null until then. Once set, it never changes.

ended_at.description: When it ended; null until then.

RunList.description: A page of runs, newest first.

has_more.description: Whether a page `starting_after` the last run here would find more.

path.description: Its path inside the run's `output/` folder, as `charts/a.png`; `output.json` is listed too.

content_type.description: Its media type, from its extension.

url.description: Where to download it. Signed fresh on every read, and it expires: re-read the run, never store a URL.

RunError.description: How a failed run ended. The run was refunded.

message.description: What happened, for a person. Branch on `code`, never on this.

RunErrorCode.description: Why a run failed. Every one is refunded.

oneOf.description: The Widget's own code crashed or wrote no output; check your input, because pressing again with the same one will likely fail the same way.
The platform's machinery failed, not the Widget; press again.
The run reached the Run Budget and was stopped; press again only with a smaller input.

ErrorResponse.description: Every failure: one `error` object, with the request's id beside it.

request_id.description: The same id as the `Request-Id` header. Quote it to support.

message.description: What to do, for a person. It may change; branch on `code`.

param.description: The Field, body key, query key or header at fault; null when the body is not a JSON object.

doc_url.description: This code on the API access page.

shortfall.description: With `insufficient_funds`: how much Byssium your wallet is short of the price.

price.description: With `price_above_max`: what the run costs now.

ErrorCode.description: Every code `/v1` sends, its HTTP status (`x-status`) and what to do. New codes may be added; treat one you don't know by its status.

oneOf.description: Send a live API Key as `Authorization: Bearer abyss_sk_…`; a missing, unknown or revoked key, or a website sign-in token, is refused, so create a new key in your Cave if this one is gone.
Check the id and the path: this key can't see that Widget or run, and a run is readable only when one of your keys made it through `/v1`.

Fix the part `param` names (null when the body is not a JSON object): a press takes only `input`, `max_price` and `wait` (a boolean), an upload only `field`, `filename` and `size`, the run list only `limit` and `starting_after`, and an `Idempotency-Key` is 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters.
Make the input match the Widget's `input_schema` (`GET /v1/widgets/{id}`), starting with the Field `param` names; the message lists every problem.
Name one of the Widget's file Fields; `param` is the name you sent.
Send a file of a type the Field `param` names takes.
Send a smaller file for the Field `param` names.
Send the id of your own upload for this Widget (`POST /v1/widgets/{id}/uploads`) in the Field `param` names.
Upload the file again and send its new id in the Field `param` names.
Send fewer files in the Field `param` names.
Send an `https` URL on a public address that answers with the file, or upload the file and send its id, in the Field `param` names.
Send a new `Idempotency-Key` for a new press; a retry must repeat the first request exactly.
Wait the `Retry-After` seconds, then send the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` again to get its run.
Top up your wallet by at least `shortfall` Ƀ, then press again.
Raise or remove this key's Spend Cap in your Cave, or wait for the next calendar month (UTC); retrying sooner will not help.
Check the new `price` (`GET /v1/widgets/{id}`), then press again with a higher `max_price` or none.
Wait the seconds in the `Retry-After` header, then send the request again.
Try again; if it keeps happening, quote the `request_id` to support.
